acceptance: A failed-jobs re-run of verify-fast-duration either re-measures or prints that it reused attempt N's timings and how to re-measure.
A PR that adds no tests reports 0 new tests against the current baseline.
The speed-factor decision is recorded with the measured runs behind it.
description:
Observed on BenchBox #4172 (2026-11-12, ci run 43254784181), a PR that changes no Python code or tests (lock, two workflow refs, review.yml, one doc, one changelog fragment):
1. `core` / verify-fast-duration failed: summed ratio 1.343 > 1.30, delta +656 s > 360 s, runner speed factor 1.635.
2. `gh run rerun --failed` re-ran only the verify job. It read the same fast-junit artifacts and printed identical numbers, so the 're-run once' recovery could not measure anything. Only a full workflow re-run re-measured: ratio 1.042, delta +80 s, speed factor 1.199, pass.
3. The verdict counted '446 new tests (58.0 s, 38.4 s over allowance)' for a PR that adds none, so the baseline lags develop and every PR is charged for tests other PRs added.
4. The speed-factor normalisation did not absorb a 1.6x slow runner.
Work:
- Make the verify job say plainly when its inputs come from an earlier attempt, and document that only a full re-run re-measures; or make the shard jobs re-run with it.
- Count as 'new' only tests the PR's own diff adds, or refresh the baseline from develop's newest merged runs.
- Review whether the speed factor should cap or widen the thresholds when it exceeds about 1.4.
Guardrails: never weaken the gate for a PR that really slows the tier (the threshold change needs measured runs); heavy-work and test-lock rules apply; changelog fragment if user-visible.
